Senses.Explanation: The term credits or tests demonstrated competence: an adept, a real hand. Yuanwu Keqin applies it to an interlocutor who handles an exchange, to an adept lineage teacher who frees people from entanglement, to a meeting conducted on adept terms, and to an adept Chan guest who acts as soon as a case is raised. Pang Yun exclaims it as direct praise. Xinghua Cunjiang compounds it with battle-general and demands a direct advance. Qingping Weikuang dismisses the approaching participant as not an adept. In a poetic exchange an unnamed interlocutor uses it with poet, showing that the competence belongs to the role supplied by context rather than defining only a Chan office. The corpus supports expert status, not the modern default sense author or writer. Independent later witnesses apply it to the means required of a teaching-seat master and even to Emperor Zhuangzong as an ‘adept ruler’; the competence follows the supplied role. A corpus-wide control for the ordinary verbs ‘compose,’ ‘write,’ and ‘compile,’ the ordinary noun ‘author,’ and the compound ‘adept poet’ found author/composer grammar named by other words, while the headword continues to predicate demonstrated capability.

Tianyin Yuanxiu uses the label for Linji Yixuan and Puhua overturning the meal table, then asks who traps the tiger and who captures the dragon. Feiyin Tongrong joins the meeting to reciprocal striking and a knowing counterpart, while Tianran Hanshi says a single statement then shows gain or loss. Tianyin Yuanxiu also applies it to Deshan Xuanjian and Guishan Lingyou while distinguishing the encounter itself from a response he judges too late. The expression is an appraisal made by the cited commentator; two masters merely occupying one narrative do not thereby become adepts meeting.

Senses.Explanation: The dead-horse cure of the Chan records: the master concedes the case is past saving and treats it anyway — speech as the last kindness, or a kindness refused. Yunfeng Wenyue rules the sickness past the poultice beyond prescribing and does the dead-horse cure anyway, asking the assembly whether there is still blood under their skin, Chaozong Tongren finds that on close inspection even the ancients' head-straight tail-straight awakenings remain dead-horse cures turned fixed things still wanting the Caoshan gate's beating, Ying'an Tanhua sets the good doctor's gate where the patients only grow worse and charges Bao'en with the cure anyway, unable to dodge the lacquer-bucket brigade, and Yongjue Yuanxian concedes he merely does the dead-horse cure in teaching people to leave mind-consciousness and pierce through to the inherent light, denying all the while that it dulls the brothers. Jiqi Hongchu grants that Lingyan cannot help but do the dead-horse cure and rules a whole life of pilgrimage just post-shaking in the mud and watching others eat, Tianran Hanshi forbids the cure outright — the second visit of Baizhang and the clapped palms of Yantou stand beyond it — Pinjixiang Zhixiang calls his own hedge-tearing wall-patching the unavoidable cure and blesses the one who would overturn the seat and shout the assembly away, and Guxue Zhenzhe rules the ancients had no choice either: mud and water at the second-meaning gate, the neither-touch-nor-turn watchword already eight characters flung open.

Chan preserves who bows, to whom, and at what turn; the action is public and timed, not an inferred inward attitude.

Senses.Explanation: This interrogative asks how something is, how one will respond, or what can be said or done: “how?” Its force is often a live demand rather than a request for exposition. Baizhang Huaihai blocks throat and lips and asks how Guishan will speak; Shitou Xiqian rejects “this way” and “not this way” and asks what his student will do; Linji Yixuan asks how the present listener proposes to cultivate, realize, or adorn the person hearing the teaching. It also follows a proposed action—“what if the foot is raised?”—asks how someone understands a case, presses “ultimately, how?”, asks how a ceremonial address should be raised, or introduces “what is the final phrase?” Dialectal spellings perform the same interrogative work in the cited passages. The phrase supplies no answer by itself; its recurring role is to force the next move.

Senses.Explanation: To calculate and guess; speculative reckoning. The graphs join ‘divine or forecast’ (卜) to ‘measure or estimate’ (度). The compound has 778 occurrences in 227 source files. Its recurrent coordinations locate the act in thinking, affective cognition, the root of thought, and mental weighing without creating additional senses. Dahui Zonggao says, in a list, ‘do not reckon under the root of thought; do not give a phrase; do not remain silent for a long time’ (不得向意根下卜度。不得下語。不得良久。). His memorial inscription says, ‘Chan, Chan: do not use thinking and conjectural calculation; it does not concern written words and speech’ (禪禪不用思量卜度。非干文字語言。). Yuanwu Keqin asks in the Blue Cliff Record whether the cited matter can be reckoned by affective cognition (以情識卜度得麼). Baoguo Zhao warns the assembly not to conjecture inside cognition because that becomes inverted imagining (莫向意識裏卜度。却成妄想顛倒。). Shaoshan Daoxin gives the compact public-interview verdict: ‘if you conjecture, you lose body and life’ (卜度則喪身失命). Zen bends an ordinary term for divinatory estimation into a recurrent name for the mental guessing explicitly rejected at the teaching seat. Yongjue Yuanxian says that conjecturing within discriminating consciousness leaves only a vaguely perceived clod; Shending Yunwai Ze groups conjecture and discursive thought with outward seeking and self-binding. Both confirm the same act of speculative assessment.

Senses.Explanation: 杜撰 means fabricated: made up without a reliable basis. Huishan Jiexian uses it openly of his own invention, saying that he 'did not shrink from fabricating' (乃不辭杜撰) before describing procedures he devised. Micang Kai condemns people who 'fabricate verses and praises' (杜撰偈讚). Dahui Zonggao asks whether an account is 'Miaoxi's fabricated speech, or has a textual basis' (這箇為復是妙喜杜撰說為復有本據), making the contrast explicit. Tian'an Sheng builds a punning dialogue around the graphs as the staff's 'surname Du, given name Zhuan' (姓杜，名撰); the staff then asks how an elder who did not fabricate could spend all day talking about Zhang and Li. A lamp preserves Fahua Quanju's rebuke that 'fabricated elders are as numerous as hemp and millet' (杜撰長老如麻似粟). Across these sources the word can describe producing material, modify the resulting speech or verse, or label a person by the same judgment; the texts do not establish separate senses for those grammatical forms.

Senses.Note: Two independent recorded-sayings witnesses retain the exact rebuke; parallel lamp recensions have been removed as padding.
